title: The Cardiff Giant Hoax
hook: Who really carved the stone giant that fooled a town?
headline: The stone giant that fooled America

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In October 1869, workers unearthed a ten-foot gypsum figure near Cardiff.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Showman P.T. Barnum advertised the giant as a petrified ancient, charging admission.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: In 1872, geologist Orson S. exposed the giant as carved gypsum by farmer William.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Later analysis matched the giant's seams to the Onondaga quarry near Syracuse.

end.line: Do you think the giant was pure profit or belief?

description: Explore the 19th-century stone giant hoax that duped America.

facts.claim: The stone figure was discovered near Cardiff, New York in October 1869.
P.T. Barnum exhibited the giant, advertising it as a petrified ancient man and charged admission.
In 1872, geologist Orson S. exposed the giant as a gypsum carving made by farmer William L.
Seam analysis linked the giant's stone to the Onondaga gypsum quarry near Syracuse.

bad: contradicted: The giant was a stone figure (spravne: gypsum figure)

contradicted: In 1872, geologist Orson S. exposed the giant as carved gypsum by farmer William (spravne: The hoax was exposed by Samuel Hull's confession in December 1869; no geologist named Orson S. in 1872)
unsupported: In October 1869, workers unearthed a ten-foot gypsum figure near Cardiff
unsupported: Later analysis matched the giant's seams to the Onondaga quarry near Syracuse
